examples.ko: 빵 한 쪽에 마요네즈를 얇게 발라요.
examples.en: I spread mayonnaise thinly on one slice of bread.
I put too much mayonnaise in the salad.
Mayonnaise always goes into potato salad.

examples.ko: 마요네즈가 다 떨어져서 마트에 가야 해요.
examples.en: We've run out of mayonnaise, so I have to go to the mart.
Once mayonnaise is opened, keep it in the fridge.

examples.ko: 저는 마요네즈에 케첩을 섞어서 찍어 먹어요.
examples.en: I mix ketchup into mayonnaise and dip my food in it.

explain: 친구끼리는 줄여서 '마요'라고도 하고, '치킨마요', '참치마요'처럼 메뉴 이름에도 붙어요. 케첩, 머스터드와 함께 '소스'라고 묶어서 부르기도 해요. 샌드위치나 샐러드에 자주 들어가요.

phrases.example: 샌드위치에 마요 좀 더 넣어 주세요.
phrases.en: Please put a little more mayo in the sandwich.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마요네즈'를 줄인 말로, 친구나 가게에서 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short, casual form of 'mayonnaise' used with friends or when ordering.

phrases.example: 저는 편의점에서 참치마요 삼각김밥을 자주 사요.
phrases.en: I often buy tuna mayo triangle kimbap at the convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마요네즈가 들어간 메뉴 이름에 붙는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A menu name for a dish made with tuna and mayonnaise.

phrases.en: I spread mayonnaise on the bread and put ham on it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빵 같은 것에 얇게 펴 놓을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for spreading mayonnaise thinly on bread or similar food.

explain_en: Friends shorten it to '마요', and it also appears in menu names like '치킨마요' (chicken mayo) and '참치마요' (tuna mayo). It is sometimes grouped with ketchup and mustard as '소스' (sauces). It goes into sandwiches and salads often.

examples.en: The child is sucking on a candy.
A mosquito sucked my blood, so my arm itches.
Insects suck the nectar from flowers.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 손가락을 빨아먹는 버릇이 있었어요.
examples.en: As a kid I had a habit of sucking on my fingers.
If you suck on ice, your mouth feels cool.
My younger sibling sucked up all the ice cream.

explain: '빨아먹다'는 입안에서 빨아서 먹는 모습을 그리는 말이에요. 사탕, 꿀, 즙처럼 빨아서 먹는 것과 잘 어울려요. 컵에 든 음료는 보통 '마시다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 사장이 직원들의 피를 빨아먹는다는 기사가 나왔어요.
phrases.en: bleed someone dry; exploit
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 힘들게 번 것을 부당하게 가져가는 사람을 비난할 때 써요. 거친 말이라 일상 대화에서는 조심해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to condemn someone who unfairly takes what others worked hard for. It is harsh, so be careful in daily talk.

explain_en: To suck on — use the mouth for candy or juice, everyday (사탕을 빨아먹다) '빨아먹다' pictures sucking something in your mouth, and it fits things like candy, nectar, or juice. A drink in a cup is usually just '마시다'.

t90.ax: The child is sucking on a candy.

examples.en: I grind coffee beans and brew coffee.
This cafe roasts its own coffee beans.
I bought a bag of coffee beans as a gift.

examples.ko: 갓 간 원두 향이 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: The smell of freshly ground coffee beans is really good.
You can keep leftover coffee beans in the freezer.

examples.ko: 원두는 신맛이 약한 걸로 골라 주세요.
examples.en: Please pick beans that are not very sour.

explain: 일상에서는 '커피콩'보다 '원두'를 더 자주 써요. 카페에서 '원두를 고르다', '원두를 갈다'처럼 말하고, 커피를 만드는 동사는 '내리다'예요. '원두커피'는 간 원두로 내린 커피를 가리켜요.

phrases.en: Every morning I grind coffee beans and drink coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 커피를 내리기 전에 원두를 가루로 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for grinding beans before brewing coffee.

phrases.en: I chose the coffee beans at the cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카페에서 어떤 원두를 쓸지 고를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for choosing which beans to use at a cafe.

phrases.en: I like coffee made from ground beans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간 원두로 내린 커피를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to coffee brewed from ground beans.

explain_en: In daily speech Koreans say 'wondu' more often than 'coffee bean' (커피콩). At a cafe you '원두를 고르다' (choose beans) or '원두를 갈다' (grind), and the verb for making coffee is '내리다' (brew). '원두커피' means coffee brewed from ground beans.

examples.en: During the trip I had breakfast at the hotel.

examples.ko: 내일 조식은 몇 시부터 먹을 수 있어요?
examples.en: From what time can I have breakfast tomorrow?
Breakfast is included at this accommodation.

examples.ko: 호텔 조식 뷔페는 음식 종류가 아주 다양해요.
examples.en: The hotel breakfast buffet has a great variety of food.
I'll come down before breakfast time ends.
If you sign up for breakfast, they bring it to your room.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '아침 먹었어요?'처럼 '아침'이라고 해요. '조식'은 호텔, 리조트, 학교와 회사 급식표에서 보이는 글말에 가까워요. 짝말은 점심 '중식', 저녁 '석식'이고, 호텔 예약에서는 '조식 포함'이라는 표시가 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This room includes breakfast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호텔 예약에서 자주 보이는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in hotel bookings.

phrases.en: Breakfast time is from 7 to 10.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호텔 안내에서 식사 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in hotel notices to give meal hours.

phrases.en: I had breakfast at the hotel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조식'보다 일상에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in daily life than 조식.

explain_en: Breakfast at hotels, resorts and menus — service wording. In everyday talk Koreans just say '아침', as in '아침 먹었어요?'. 조식 is closer to written language, seen at hotels, resorts, and on school and company meal schedules. Its partners are 중식 (lunch) and 석식 (dinner), and hotel bookings often show '조식 포함' (breakfast included).

t90.ax: I'll come down before breakfast time ends.

examples.ko: 제가 간단한 마술을 하나 보여 줄게요.
examples.en: I will show you a simple magic trick.

examples.ko: 아이들이 마술 쇼를 보고 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The children watched the magic show and clapped.
My uncle is very interested in magic.
Something like magic happened.
Magic is a trick, but it is amazing to watch.
I am curious about the secret of that trick.

explain: 마술은 속임수로 신기하게 보여 주는 공연이고, '마법'은 이야기 속의 진짜 힘이에요. 그래서 쇼에서는 '마술', 동화나 게임에서는 '마법'을 써요.

phrases.example: 그 마술사는 카드를 아주 잘 다뤄요.
phrases.en: That magician handles cards very well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마술을 직업으로 하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who performs magic tricks as a job.

phrases.en: I'm learning magic these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마술 기술을 익히는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you are learning how to do magic tricks.

phrases.en: The ball suddenly disappeared, so it felt like magic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿기 힘들 만큼 신기한 일을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for something so amazing it is hard to believe.

explain_en: Tricks performed by a magician — shows, cards, entertainment. 마술 is a performance that amazes with tricks, while '마법' is real power in a story. So shows use '마술', and fairy tales or games use '마법'.

examples.en: The children are wrestling in the playground.
Yesterday I wrestled with my uncle.
We will wrestle with family during the holiday.
The wrestlers are standing on the sand ring.

examples.ko: 우리는 한참 씨름하고 나서 땀을 닦았어요.
examples.en: After wrestling for a good while, we wiped off our sweat.
My arm hurts because I wrestled with my brother.

explain: 한국 전통 운동 '씨름'에서 나온 말이에요. 명사 '씨름'은 '씨름을 하다'와 '씨름하다' 두 가지로 모두 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 저는 어제 하루 종일 숙제와 씨름했어요.
phrases.en: struggle with something for a long time
phrases.nuance_ko: 어렵거나 잘 풀리지 않는 일을 오래 붙잡고 애쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you keep working at something hard that won't come together.

explain_en: It comes from the traditional Korean sport 씨름. The noun can be used either as 씨름을 하다 or joined as 씨름하다.

examples.en: The children folded a crane out of paper.
I go to a paper folding class every weekend.
Doing paper folding works as practice for your hands.

examples.ko: 종이접기는 색종이 한 장만 있으면 시작할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can start paper folding with just one sheet of colored paper.
I borrowed a book about paper folding from the library.

examples.ko: 동생은 종이접기도 잘하고 그림도 잘 그려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is good at paper folding and drawing too.

explain: '종이를 접다'에서 나온 말이라서 '종이접기를 하다'라고 해요. 접는 종이는 보통 '색종이'를 많이 써요. 접어서 만든 것은 '학', '종이배'처럼 이름을 따로 불러요.

phrases.en: On weekends I do paper folding with my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이접기를 한다고 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say you do paper folding.

phrases.en: The paper folding class is really fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이접기를 배우는 시간이나 모임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a class or lesson for paper folding.

phrases.example: 색종이로 종이접기를 하면 예쁜 것을 만들 수 있어요.
phrases.en: With colored paper, you can make pretty things by folding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 종이를 쓰는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what kind of paper is used.

explain_en: It comes from '종이를 접다', so you say '종이접기를 하다'. The paper used is often '색종이' (colored paper). What you make is called by its own name, such as '학' (crane) or '종이배' (paper boat).

examples.en: I played card games with my family during the holiday.
Card games have simple rules, so you learn them quickly.
My friends are totally hooked on card games.

examples.ko: 카드놀이 하다가 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was playing cards and lost track of time.

examples.ko: 카드놀이로 내기를 하면 항상 제가 져요.
examples.en: When we bet on card games, I always lose.

examples.ko: 카드놀이가 재미있어서 여행 갈 때도 카드를 가져가요.
examples.en: Card games are fun, so I bring cards when I travel too.

explain: 트럼프 카드로 하는 놀이를 말해요. 화투로 하는 '고스톱'은 따로 부르고, '카드놀이'라고 하면 보통 트럼프 카드를 떠올려요.

phrases.en: I played a card game with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '카드놀이'와 비슷하고, 놀이보다 게임이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'card play', with more of a 'game' feel.

phrases.en: I won at the card game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 말할 때 '이기다/지다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'win/lose' to talk about the result.

phrases.en: Shall we play cards together?
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 하자고 부드럽게 제안할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to suggest playing together.

explain_en: It refers to games played with a deck of playing cards. Games played with 화투 flower cards, like '고스톱', are named separately, and '카드놀이' usually makes people think of regular playing cards.

examples.ko: 가을철에는 일교차가 커서 감기에 걸리기 쉬워요.
examples.en: In autumn the temperature gap between day and night is big, so it's easy to catch a cold.
When autumn comes, the leaves change color on every mountain.

examples.ko: 가을철 별미로 밤과 고구마를 많이 먹어요.
examples.en: People eat a lot of chestnuts and sweet potatoes as autumn treats.
Autumn has nice weather, so it's good for traveling.

examples.ko: 가을철엔 낮과 밤의 온도 차이가 커요.
examples.en: In autumn, the temperature difference between day and night is large.
With autumn here, the number of hikers has jumped.

explain: '철'은 어떤 계절이나 시기를 말해서, '가을철'은 가을이라는 기간을 가리켜요. 하루를 말하는 '가을날'과 달리 건강이나 안전을 알리는 뉴스와 안내문에 자주 나와요. '봄철, 여름철, 겨울철'도 같은 식으로 써요.

phrases.en: You need to take care of your health in autumn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강 안내에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in health advice.

phrases.en: Autumn weather is clear and cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절 전체의 날씨를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the weather of the whole season.

phrases.en: There are many autumn events, so I'm busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절 동안 열리는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for things held during the season.

explain_en: '철' refers to a season or period, so '가을철' points to the autumn period as a whole. Unlike '가을날', which means one day, it often appears in news and notices about health or safety. '봄철, 여름철, 겨울철' work the same way.

t90.ax: With autumn here, the number of hikers has jumped.

examples.en: Please don't touch my desk.
The child bumped the vase and it broke.
If you poke the sleeping cat, it will get angry.
My younger sibling keeps messing with my phone.
Who touched my bag?

examples.ko: 남의 물건을 건들고 가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't touch other people's things and leave.

explain: '건드리다'를 줄인 말이라서 대화에서 자주 들려요. 물건이나 몸을 살짝 만질 때도 쓰고, 상대를 일부러 자극하거나 시비를 걸 때도 써요.

phrases.en: Please don't touch my desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '건들다'의 원래 형태이고, 글에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 'geondeulda', usable in writing too.

phrases.en: Don't touch my bag!
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족에게 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech used with friends or family.

phrases.en: I touched the door lightly and it opened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세게 말고 가볍게 만질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a light touch, not a hard one.

explain_en: Casual spoken — touch or mess with things, often unwanted (남의 물건을 건들다) It is a shortened form of '건드리다' and is heard often in conversation. It can mean lightly touching things or the body, and also deliberately provoking someone.

examples.en: I scooped the soup with a ladle into a bowl.
The ladle fell into the pot and I am looking for it.
Buy a ladle with a long handle.
I stirred the stew using a ladle.
Please give me one more ladle.
The soup in the ladle was hot.

explain: 국이나 찌개를 뜰 때는 '국자', 밥을 뜰 때는 '주걱', 먹을 때는 '숟가락'을 써요. 모두 '뜨다'와 비슷하게 쓰지만 도구가 달라요.

phrases.en: I slowly stirred the stew with a ladle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨는 것뿐 아니라 섞을 때도 국자를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A ladle is used not only for scooping but also for stirring.

phrases.en: There is a lot of soup, so I need a big ladle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 말할 때 '큰', '작은'을 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 큰 or 작은 before it to describe the size.

phrases.en: I bought one ladle for the kitchen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 셀 때 '하나'를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 하나 to count one item.

explain_en: A '국자' is for scooping soup or stew, a '주걱' is for scooping rice, and a '숟가락' is for eating. They all go with a scooping action, but the tools are different.

examples.en: I turned the radio dial and made the sound louder.

examples.ko: 다이얼이 고장 나서 문이 안 열려요.
examples.en: The dial is broken, so the door will not open.
Old phones used a dial to enter the number.
Please turn the oven dial to the right.

examples.ko: 할아버지 집에는 다이얼 전화기가 아직 있어요.
examples.en: My grandfather's house still has a dial phone.

examples.ko: 작은 다이얼도 하나 있고 버튼도 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: There is one small dial and two buttons too.

explain: '다이얼을 돌리다'처럼 돌리는 동작과 같이 써요. 버튼은 누르고 다이얼은 돌려요. 전화를 걸 때는 보통 '전화를 걸다'라고 하고, 다이얼은 옛날 돌리는 전화기를 이야기할 때 나와요.

phrases.en: My grandmother's house has a dial phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날에 번호를 돌려서 걸던 전화기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to old phones where you turn a dial to call.

phrases.en: Turn the volume dial to the right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 조절하는 돌리는 손잡이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A turning knob that controls the sound.

phrases.en: I set the dial to the number.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하는 자리에 오도록 돌릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when turning the dial to the position you want.

explain_en: It goes with the action of turning, as in '다이얼을 돌리다'. You press a '버튼' but you turn a 다이얼. To make a phone call people normally say '전화를 걸다', and 다이얼 comes up when talking about old rotary phones.

examples.ko: 식사가 끝나면 다 같이 뒷정리를 해요.
examples.en: After the meal, we all clean up together.
I'll do the party cleanup tomorrow.

examples.ko: 마지막까지 남은 사람이 뒷정리를 하고 가야 해요.
examples.en: The person who stays until the end has to tidy up before leaving.
Thank you so much for helping even with the cleanup.

examples.ko: 아이들이 놀고 난 뒤 뒷정리가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Tidying up after the kids have played is tough.

examples.ko: 캠핑이 끝나고 뒷정리에 한 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: After camping, the cleanup took an hour.

explain: 일이나 행사가 끝난 뒤 어질러진 곳을 치우고 정돈하는 걸 말해요. 일 자체를 마무리하는 '뒤처리'와 달리 물건을 치우는 느낌이 강해요. '뒷정리를 하다'로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: After the party, I helped clean up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치우는 일을 같이 해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when helping with the cleanup.

phrases.en: I'll take care of the cleanup today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치우는 일을 책임지고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you take charge of the cleanup.

phrases.en: When the cleanup is done, we go home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치우는 일이 끝났다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the cleaning up is finished.

explain_en: It means tidying up the mess after a task or event is over. Unlike '뒤처리', which is about finishing off the matter itself, it mainly feels like putting things away. It is commonly used as '뒷정리를 하다'.
